subject.title: [Feature]: Built-in headless browser for reliable web access without external dependencies

question: Should OpenClaw make rendered browser-backed extraction/search a first-class web-access path, or keep browser automation as a separate tool and route only narrower runtime gaps to existing browser/search issues?
rationale: The missing capability is source-proven, but the fix changes security, session, proxy, packaging, and tool-routing semantics that automation cannot safely choose.

options.title: Design browser-backed web access
options.body: Keep this issue open as the product/security tracker and split approved implementation into narrow PRs for rendered extraction, session persistence, proxy policy, and runtime packaging.

options.title: Keep browser separate
options.body: Decline a unified web_fetch/web_search browser fallback and route individual runtime gaps to existing browser-tool issues.

options.title: Move extraction to plugins
options.body: Require browser-backed extraction to be provided by a plugin or external provider unless core/plugin APIs are proven insufficient.

recommendation.title: Design browser-backed web access
recommendation.body: Keep this issue open as the product/security tracker and split approved implementation into narrow PRs for rendered extraction, session persistence, proxy policy, and runtime packaging.

likelyOwner.reason: The strongest history for the browser boundary and docs points here for product-direction routing.
